forces.title: Strengthening construction activity across commercial and civil engineering
forces.description: Ireland's construction sector is experiencing a broad-based recovery, with sustained new order inflows leading to strengthening activity. Commercial construction and civil engineering are showing the strongest growth, reaching their highest levels since 2022. This upward trend in these construction segments directly boosts demand for Cement & Concrete Products, providing a significant tailwind for the industry's sales volumes and overall activity in Ireland.

forces.title: Persistently low construction activity dampening growth in Norway
forces.description: Norwegian construction activity remains low, characterized by few new residential and commercial projects, despite some regional exceptions. This ongoing weakness dampens order volumes for architects, consultants, and building materials manufacturers, directly reducing demand for Cement & Concrete Products. The repeated postponement of an upturn in residential construction, largely due to high interest rates and rising building costs, exacerbates this headwind.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: European construction sector returns to growth after two challenging years
forces.description: After a decline in 2024 and stagnation in 2025, the European construction sector is set to return to growth in 2026 with a projected 1.5% increase in production. This cyclical rebound, driven by improving confidence, increasing housing permits, and infrastructure investments, will translate into renewed demand for Cement & Concrete Products across the EU, marking a positive shift from recent challenging economic conditions.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

forces.title: Shift in building materials M&A to scope/capability expansion
forces.description: The center of gravity in building products M&A, including cement, is shifting from traditional scale plays towards scope and capability expansion. This is due to high market concentration, particularly in the cement sector where opportunities for large-scale consolidation have diminished. Companies are now pursuing acquisitions to access new product categories, customer segments, or complementary building materials, which represents a fundamental change in growth strategy for Cement & Concrete Products players.

forces.title: European Affordable Housing Plan boosts construction demand
forces.description: The European Affordable Housing Plan, published in December 2025, aims to add 650,000 extra homes annually across the EU to address housing shortages. This coordinated response, coupled with a strategy to make the construction industry more competitive and promote sustainable materials, will significantly increase demand for Cement & Concrete Products. The plan also includes EIB financing for new technologies to reduce construction costs.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

forces.title: Elevated energy prices increase input costs for cement production
forces.description: The ongoing Middle East conflict and resulting volatility in global oil and gas markets have driven up energy prices. For energy-intensive industries like Cement & Concrete Products, particularly clinker production, higher energy costs translate directly into increased operating expenses and margin pressure. This external geopolitical risk remains a critical cost input challenge, impacting the profitability of European cement manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Construction cost inflation and planning constraints hinder new builds
forces.description: In Ireland, construction cost inflation, along with planning and regulatory constraints, is a significant headwind, leading to a more cautious investment environment. Capital investment in sectors like healthcare is prioritizing refurbishment and energy efficiency upgrades over new-build expansion. This shift away from new construction projects, driven by rising costs and bureaucratic hurdles, reduces the potential demand for new Cement & Concrete Products.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: AI reshaping AEC industry to improve productivity and efficiency
forces.description: Artificial intelligence is poised to rewire the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry, with the potential to automate significant nonphysical work and unlock substantial value (estimated at $126 billion annually in Europe by 2030 for construction alone). This adoption of AI for design, modeling, and construction-feasibility workflows will lead to improved efficiency and productivity across the entire value chain, creating an upside driver for optimizing demand and use of Cement & Concrete Products.
forces.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of the AEC industry

forces.title: Energy supply development and data centre buildout boost construction
forces.description: Investments in energy supply development and the rapid buildout of data centers are identified as important growth drivers for the Norwegian economy, and specifically for construction activity. These large-scale infrastructure projects directly stimulate demand for heavy construction materials, including Cement & Concrete Products, partially offsetting the general low activity in residential and commercial building construction.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Germany's €500bn infrastructure plan and climate investments
forces.description: Germany has introduced a €500 billion plan for infrastructure and climate investments, which is expected to drive a gradual recovery in the construction sector. This significant public investment, partly a reallocation from the regular budget, will specifically boost demand for heavy materials like cement and concrete, particularly for railway projects, though bureaucratic hurdles may delay substantial market impact until late 2026.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

forces.title: Nitrogen emission regulations hinder Dutch construction projects
forces.description: The Dutch-specific nitrogen issue, where new building projects often require permits proving they will not increase nitrogen emissions, is causing significant project postponements and cancellations. This regulatory bottleneck, alongside other structural challenges like grid congestion and complex permitting, severely dampens housing and general construction activity, creating a substantial headwind for demand in Cement & Concrete Products in the Netherlands.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

forces.title: Building material costs stabilize, improving new housing business case
forces.description: After significant disruptions, building material costs have largely stopped rising in Europe, improving the business case for new housing projects. Combined with increasing wages and rising housing prices, this stability makes new residential developments more attractive. This cyclical easing of cost pressure provides a tailwind for the construction sector and, consequently, for the demand and profitability of Cement & Concrete Products.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

forces.title: Renovation and sustainability investments drive construction demand
forces.description: The specialized construction sector, including both residential and non-residential segments, is increasingly benefiting from investments in renovation and sustainability works. Energy efficiency requirements and sustainability incentives encourage upgrades and modernizations, providing a counterbalancing force to slower new build activity. This shift fuels demand for Cement & Concrete Products suitable for refurbishment and eco-friendly construction, creating a new source of growth.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

viewpoints.title: European construction sector set for 1.5% growth in 2026 after stagnation
viewpoints.description: The European construction sector is projected to return to growth in 2026, with production expected to increase by 1.5% after declining in 2024 and stagnating in 2025. This optimistic outlook is supported by improving confidence among contractors, an increase in permits for new housing, and additional infrastructure investments. While the building sector faced headwinds from higher interest rates and increased costs in previous years, renovation, sustainability works, and infrastructure projects are now providing counterbalance, which is positive for Cement & Concrete Products.
viewpoints.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

viewpoints.title: Ireland's construction activity strengthening, led by commercial and civil engineering
viewpoints.description: Construction activity in Ireland continues to strengthen for a third consecutive month, driven by sustained new order inflows across the sector. Growth is broad-based, with employment rising and commercial construction seeing the strongest expansion. Civil engineering activity is at its highest level since 2022. Although housing remains the weakest segment due to taxation and rent-cap policies, strong underlying demand is expected to support long-term activity. This positive trend in overall construction is a significant tailwind for the Cement & Concrete Products sector.

viewpoints.title: Norwegian construction activity remains low, delaying residential upturn
viewpoints.description: Construction activity in Norway continues to be low, with few new residential and commercial projects reported. While some contacts in the South-West region note a pickup in residential construction, many others believe a broader upturn is continually delayed. This low activity is dampening growth across the construction sector, including for building materials manufacturers, posing a challenge for the Cement & Concrete Products industry, although state-level projects are increasing.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Dutch building volumes face low growth and chronic structural bottlenecks
viewpoints.description: The Netherlands is expected to see low growth rates in building volumes, with a projected increase of just 0.5% in both 2025 and 2026, following a 2.9% contraction in 2024. Housing construction is particularly weak due to a shortage of building land, complex permitting requirements, objection procedures, grid congestion, and the nitrogen emission issue. These chronic bottlenecks continue to cause project postponements and cancellations, creating significant headwinds for the Cement & Concrete Products sector in the country.
viewpoints.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

viewpoints.title: German construction sector anticipates recovery in 2026 after multi-year decline
viewpoints.description: Germany's construction industry, the largest in Europe, is projected to return to growth in 2026 with a 2.5% increase, after contracting by over 10% between 2020 and 2025. This anticipated recovery is driven by a gradual rebound in the new residential market and increased infrastructure investment. Government initiatives like the 'housing construction turbo' aim to expedite planning and authorization of new projects. This outlook is cautiously positive for Cement & Concrete Products, signaling potential demand recovery.
viewpoints.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

viewpoints.title: Spanish construction poised for robust growth driven by permits and GDP
viewpoints.description: The Spanish construction sector is expected to achieve 2.5% growth in 2026, continuing its recovery since 2023 following a significant decline between 2019 and 2022. This positive momentum is underpinned by a surge in building permits issued in recent years, strong contractor confidence, and robust GDP growth. The favorable economic conditions and increased permit activity suggest a positive outlook for demand in the Cement & Concrete Products sector in Spain.
viewpoints.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

viewpoints.title: Belgian building permits decline despite VAT incentives for rebuilding
viewpoints.description: Belgium continues to experience a decline in the number of building permits issued, attributed to time-consuming project procedures. Despite a reduced VAT rate of 6% for demolishing and reconstructing homes (compared to 21% for new builds), which aims to stimulate activity, the overall permit situation remains challenging. This suggests ongoing headwinds for new construction demand, impacting the Cement & Concrete Products market in Belgium, with a potential shift towards renovation-led activity.
viewpoints.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

viewpoints.title: Heavy building materials show ROIC improvement despite market challenges
viewpoints.description: The heavy building materials segment (including cement, concrete, and aggregates) demonstrated resilience and improved financial performance between 2022 and 2024. While light materials saw their Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) decrease by four percentage points, heavy materials companies increased their ROIC by two percentage points, from 12% to 14%. This divergence is attributed to the stability of public funding for heavy infrastructure projects, contrasting with the impact of higher interest rates and construction costs on light materials. This indicates a positive underlying trend for Cement & Concrete Products.
viewpoints.source_title: Building materials: Understanding the keys to outperformance

viewpoints.title: European building products M&A value drops, shifting to scope and capability plays
viewpoints.description: M&A activity in European construction and building products (including cement) experienced a significant drop in deal value, decreasing by 48% in the first nine months of 2025. The market is increasingly concentrated, particularly in the cement category, where traditional scale deals are largely exhausted. This leads to a strategic shift towards scope or capability expansion, with companies like Holcim targeting complementary building materials. This suggests a more challenging M&A environment focused on diversification rather than pure scale for Cement & Concrete Products.

viewpoints.title: AI adoption to unlock significant value in European construction by 2030
viewpoints.description: Artificial intelligence is expected to meaningfully reshape the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) sector. In Europe, AI could unlock roughly $126 billion in annual value in the construction sector alone by 2030. Early adopters are already reporting productivity gains from design, modeling, and construction-feasibility workflows. While AI won't solve all productivity challenges, it offers potential to automate significant nonphysical work, transforming workflows and data use, which will structurally impact the demand dynamics and operational efficiency within the Cement & Concrete Products value chain.
viewpoints.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of the AEC industry

demand_drivers.description: EU plan to add 650,000 new homes annually on top of 1.6 million current builds, directly increasing demand for all construction materials.
The plan promotes sustainable and energy-efficient housing, implying demand for specific, advanced cement and concrete product formulations.

new_opportunities.description: The European Affordable Housing Plan aims to significantly boost housing supply, creating substantial, sustained demand for cement and concrete products.

market_sizing.methodology: The European Affordable Housing Plan outlines a target to add 650,000 extra homes annually across the EU, supplementing the current 1.6 million homes built per year. This initiative, driven by housing shortages and social stability concerns, will directly increase demand for construction materials, including cement and concrete products. The strategy also promotes sustainable and energy-efficient housing, indicating a focus on quality and specific material specifications.
market_sizing.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

demand_drivers.description: Stable public funding for infrastructure projects provides a resilient demand base for heavy materials like cement and concrete, insulating them from some economic fluctuations.

pnl_drivers.description: ROIC for heavy materials companies increased by 2 percentage points from 12% to 14% between 2022 and 2024, indicating improved profitability and capital efficiency compared to light materials.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of 102 publicly listed building materials companies in North America and Europe found that the heavy building materials segment, which explicitly includes cement, concrete, and aggregates, saw a 2 percentage point increase in ROIC from 2022 to 2024 (from 12% to 14%). This improved performance is attributed to the stability of public funding for heavy infrastructure projects, providing a more resilient revenue stream compared to light materials.
market_sizing.source_title: Building materials: Understanding the keys to outperformance

new_opportunities.description: Given high market concentration, cement companies are increasingly pursuing M&A for scope or capability expansion, like acquiring complementary building materials, rather than pure scale plays.

market_sizing.methodology: The report highlights the highly consolidated nature of the cement category in the US, where the top six players control approximately 65% to 70% of capacity, with Europe showing a similar competitive landscape. This concentration implies limited scope for traditional scale-driven M&A, pushing companies towards scope or capability expansion to drive growth.

demand_drivers.description: €9.25 billion committed to health infrastructure under the National Development Plan (2026-2030) drives demand for construction materials for refurbishments and upgrades.

new_opportunities.description: Capital investment in existing healthcare facilities, including energy efficiency upgrades, presents opportunities for specialized cement and concrete products for renovation projects.

market_sizing.methodology: The National Development Plan (2026 – 2030) commits €9.25 billion to health infrastructure. While capital investment in healthcare is currently focused on improving existing facilities rather than new builds, this significant public funding represents a substantial, ongoing demand driver for construction materials, including Cement & Concrete Products, especially for refurbishment and upgrades.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026
